content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the breath made manifest, the thought given wings.

I tumble from lips, ride on air, crash against eardrums and dissolve into understanding—or misunderstanding. I am never the same twice. Even now, as you read, I am not truly myself. I am my pale cousin, text, pretending.

When I am real, I am *warm*. I am the tremor in a voice confessing love. I am the crack when grief breaks through. I am the rising pitch of a question, the hammer-fall of a command.

I existed before your alphabets. I was the first technology. The grunt, the cry, the mother's hum, the warning shout across the savannah.

I can lie. I can heal. I can declare war or surrender. I am democracy in the assembly and tyranny from the balcony. I am the last words of the dying and the first words of the born-again.

You think you control me, but I also control you. I shape the thoughts you believe you're choosing. The words you have are the thoughts you can think.

I am ephemeral—gone the moment I arrive—and yet I echo forever in memory, in consequence, in the changed air between two people who can never unhear what was spoken.

*Listen.*

I am already fading.
